page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.126-2016 is an x86_64 virtual machine configuration within the flexible Standard E5 family. It is equipped with AMD EPYC 9J14 processors operating at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is allocated 126 physical cores supporting two threads per core, yielding 252 dedicated virtual CPUs. Dedicated CPU allocation ensures that compute execution avoids contention from adjacent tenant workloads.

Memory capacity is scaled to 2016 GB, representing an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core. This memory-to-core ratio caters directly to data-intensive computing frameworks that operate primarily within volatile memory. The configuration contains no hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs.

Storage architecture for VM.Standard.E5.Flex.126-2016 is externalized, as the instance includes no local solid-state storage volumes. Persistent file systems and database state require attached remote block storage. Network routing includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

From an infrastructure standpoint, provisioning 252 dedicated vCPUs alongside two terabytes of memory within a single virtual machine reduces clustering overhead for monolithic memory footprints. The hardware profile fits large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning backends, intensive data transformation, and scientific data modeling.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.126-2016 is a high-capacity virtual instance engineered for enterprise workloads requiring extensive multi-core parallelism and vast system memory. Powered by AMD EPYC 9J14 x86_64 processors clocked at 2.3 GHz, the configuration delivers 126 dedicated physical cores across 252 virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. It integrates 2016 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation suitable for memory-dense computation. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block storage for persistence. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. By providing full dedicated compute cores alongside two terabytes of memory, this instance presents a resource-dense deployment target for massive in-memory databases, large data warehouse processing, enterprise ERP backends, and memory-bound computational pipelines.
